pr.title: Build and find stacks with gh stack, and fall back to base branches without it
pr.head: 214027c49e4b50b90f49eded342fc4232487b58d

summary: Projector's skills tell an agent how to build a change (implement), how to answer review findings on it (fix-pr), and how to keep doing that across many pull requests (start-fix-loop). When a change is too big for one review, the agent splits it into a stack: a chain of pull requests, each based on the branch of the one below it, that GitHub records as one stack. GitHub only records the chain when it is made with gh stack, a GitHub CLI extension that Projector documents in its vendored skills/gh-stack/SKILL.md.

Before this change, only implement pointed at that extension. fix-pr said to use "the installed stack workflow" without naming it, start-fix-loop grouped a stack's pull requests without saying how to find them, and no skill said what to do when the extension is missing. In practice, agents chained pull requests with gh pr create --base, which GitHub does not record as a stack.

This change gives implement one section, "Stack dependent work", that names the gh stack commands for each task and one fallback for when gh stack cannot help. Inside a stack that gh stack works on, a layer takes in its base only by rebasing, because gh stack has no option to merge. A chain without gh stack is updated by merging, so it needs no force-push. The other skills and the repository's own docs point at that section instead of describing stacks themselves. The change is prose only: no code, test, or generated file moves.

cards.title: When a skill falls back to base branches
cards.html:
• gh extension list shows no github/gh-stack.
  • A gh stack command exits 9, which means the repository does not have stacks enabled.
  • The stacks API, repos/<owner>/<repo>/stacks?pull_request=<n>, returns an error or [].

The fallback reads the chain from each pull request's base branch, opens layers with gh pr create --draft --base, and updates layers by merging each into the one above it. The agent tells the user at most once, and never installs the extension.

cards.title: What the review found
cards.html:
• Two heads reviewed so far. One finding is still open at this head: fix-pr's conflict path sends a stack layer to implement's "Update it by rebasing" bullet, which pushes the rebased layers before fix-pr's full gate runs. See the flag under skills/fix-pr/SKILL.md.
  • The command names, flags, exit code 9, and cited section names match skills/gh-stack/SKILL.md and gh stack v0.1.0's --help.
  • The test suite, project check, and both claude plugin validate runs pass at this head.

groups.title: One place that says how to stack
groups.kicker: The new "Stack dependent work" section in implement, which every other skill now cites
intro: implement is the skill an agent follows to build a change and open its pull request. Its new "Stack dependent work" section is the reference the rest of this pull request points at. It covers four tasks, each first with gh stack and then without it.

TaskWith gh stackWithout it
Create a stackinit, add, then submit --auto, which opens draftsgit push -u, then gh pr create --draft --base per layer
Adopt an existing chaingh stack link with the pull request numbers, bottom firstNot needed
Carry a fix uprebase --upstack, then push; sync after a layer mergesMerge each layer into the one above it, from the bottom up
Take in the base or the default branchgh stack rebase, then push; never a mergeMerge the default branch into the bottom layer, then carry it up
Find the layersThe stacks API, or gh stack view --json in a checkout that tracks the stackFollow base branches with gh pr list --head and --base
The section keeps the mechanics of each command in skills/gh-stack/SKILL.md, which this pull request does not change.

files.note: Adds the "Stack dependent work" section, links to it from the sizing rule, and says to replace the body gh stack submit writes.

checks.text: The stacks API behaves as described. stacks?pull_request=196 returned stack 199 with pull requests 196 and 197 from the bottom up, including merged ones. stacks?pull_request=215 returned [], and so did the same query against cli/cli, a repository without stacks, rather than an error.
This step pushes every rebased layer before anything reruns the gate on it. That order matches fix-pr on main, so the review listed it as a suggestion rather than a finding.
The layers above a pull request come one level at a time: gh pr list --base <headRefName> finds the direct child, and the agent repeats the lookup from that child's head branch to reach the top.

Without gh stack, a chain is updated by merging rather than rebasing, the same way fix-pr updates any branch. A merge needs no force-push, so review threads stay anchored, and fix-pr's force-push rule now allows a force-push only through gh stack or where the repository's instructions call for a rebase.

groups.title: Fixing and grouping stacked pull requests
groups.kicker: fix-pr and start-fix-loop now name gh stack and cite the implement section
intro: fix-pr answers review findings and resolves merge conflicts on one pull request. start-fix-loop watches many pull requests and gives each one, or each stack, a subagent that runs fix-pr. Both used to describe stacks vaguely. Now both cite the "Stack dependent work" section for how to find a stack's layers and how to carry a fix up through them.

The main behavior change is in fix-pr's conflict handling. For an ordinary pull request, or a chain without gh stack, it still merges the base, because a merge needs no force-push. For a layer of a stack that gh stack works on, it follows implement's "Update it by rebasing" instead, because gh stack has no option to merge. Its force-push rule now allows a force-push only through gh stack, or where the repository's instructions call for a rebase.

files.note: Updates a conflicted stack layer by gh stack's rebase, carries fixes up through the implement section, syncs after a parent merges, and narrows the force-push rule.

checks.text: Open review finding, not addressed at this head. Step 1 sends a stack layer to implement's "Update it by rebasing" bullet, which says to run gh stack rebase and then gh stack push. An agent that follows it pushes every rebased layer before the step 3 gate runs, and step 4 still says to commit a merge that this path never made. The fix is to stop after the rebase in step 1 and push with gh stack push in step 4, after the gate passes.

skills/gh-stack/SKILL.md has both cited sections, "Squash-merge recovery" and "Handle rebase conflicts". Its sync description says it rebases the layers above onto the new base and skips a squash-merged parent's commits.

files.note: Finds a stack's layers, and groups pull requests into one subagent per stack, with the implement section's lookup.

groups.title: Repository instructions and plugin docs
groups.kicker: AGENTS.md and docs/plugins.md say the same thing as the skills
intro: AGENTS.md holds this repository's contributor instructions, and CLAUDE.md is a symlink to it. Its hand-over rules now say to build a stack with gh stack and to chain pull requests by base branch only where gh stack is unavailable. docs/plugins.md tells a plugin user that the extension is optional and how to install it. Neither edit touches the block between projector:begin markers that project init generates.
